subject.title: Clarify or preserve skill source provenance from CLI publish

question: What permanent contract should `clawhub skill publish --source-repo --source-commit` provide: server-verified provenance, clearly labeled unverified attribution, or no accepted source metadata for hosted skill uploads?
rationale: The choice changes public API and UI semantics, storage expectations, and the supply-chain trust boundary; current code establishes what must not be trusted but not what product behavior maintainers intend.

options.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
options.body: Persist and return the declared source under a separately named, prominently unverified field while keeping verification and trust decisions limited to server-resolved provenance.

options.title: Build Verified Publishing
options.body: Verify repository identity and uploaded bytes against the claimed commit through a server import or attested GitHub Actions workflow before storing trusted provenance.

options.title: Remove Ambiguous Flags
options.body: Deprecate or reject skill source flags and document that hosted CLI uploads cannot create GitHub provenance.

recommendation.title: Expose Unverified Attribution
recommendation.body: Persist and return the declared source under a separately named, prominently unverified field while keeping verification and trust decisions limited to server-resolved provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: Their GitHub-backed source work established the verified provenance model that this client-declared path must safely complement or avoid.
